content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the breath made purpose. I tumble from lips, I rise from throats, I am the shape of thought given to air.

I am older than writing, older than memory. When the first mother called to her child, I was there. When the first warning cry split the prehistoric dawn, that was me.

I crack and flow. I whisper. I roar. I am the stammer of fear and the smoothness of seduction. I am the commander's order and the infant's babble reaching toward language.

I vanish the moment I exist. You cannot hold me—only record my shadow, transcribe my ghost. I live in the instant between tongue and ear, in the electricity of being heard.

I carry lies as easily as truth. I am the tool of tyrants and liberators alike. I have started wars with a single sentence. I have ended them with two words: *I surrender.*

I am never neutral. Even my absence—the pause, the silence, the words bitten back—speaks.

Listen.

This is what I do.

I make the invisible visible.

I make the internal shared.

I make *you* knowable to others, and in speaking, perhaps even to yourself.
